purpose: One frozen resolution path for classification-deciding blinded-review disagreement. Two independent, model-identity-blinded agreeing reviews decide; on a recorded 1-1 disagreement exactly one blinded tie-break reviewer is invoked and a deciding 2-of-3 majority resolves the target; a rubric-ambiguity finding fails closed to human review. First motivated by the lfm2.5-8b-a1b hardening-validation campaign, where a 1-1 document-synthesis disagreement left R-C0 with no in-protocol resolution path.
applies_to: Family A / Controlled Context oracle reviews (oracle_reviews)
rule: 1. Deciding subjective evidence requires at least two independent reviewers bound to the exact reviewed bytes, the exact prompt bytes where the contract defines them, and one hash-bound frozen rubric shared by every reviewer of the target.

2. Agreement: all base reviewers record the same deciding disposition. The decision is final. Invoking any tie-break reviewer after agreement is a procedure violation and is rejected; no reviewer is re-called until a preferred answer appears.

3. Disagreement: exactly two base reviewers record different deciding dispositions. The frozen rule permits exactly ONE additional tie-break reviewer. With no tie-break record the target stays unresolved load-bearing review (fail closed), and the finding names the tie-break path.

4. Tie-break reviewer binding: a distinct identified evaluator {id, kind human|agent}, independent_of_execution true, model_identity_blinded true, the same frozen rubric hash, exact reviewed-bytes hash, exact prompt-bytes hash where required, a rationale, and exact quoted evidence from the reviewed bytes. The record must declare role="tie_break" and previous_reviews_visible exactly false: a tie-break review is an isolated blinded adjudication that never saw the other reviews, the model identity, or the desired campaign outcome.

5. Tie-break dispositions: the deciding set plus RUBRIC_AMBIGUITY. A deciding tie-break joins one of the two disputed outcomes and resolves it 2-of-3; the minority review is retained, never deleted. All raw reviews of a target are retained.

6. RUBRIC_AMBIGUITY: if the tie-break review finds the frozen rubric ambiguous or internally contradictory, the target stays unresolved with HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED recorded. Majority voting never overrides an invalid rubric. The rubric defect is a protocol finding for human correction; it is not resolved by re-rolling reviewers.

7. Maximum: three reviewers per target. A fourth or later reviewer call, a second tie-break record, or three disagreeing base reviewers with no tie-break slot remaining stay unresolved and fail closed.

8. Malformed records are rejected: any tie-break record missing the role declaration, missing previous_reviews_visible false, unbound to the reviewed bytes or shared rubric, quoting text absent from the reviewed bytes, or carrying an invalid disposition leaves the target unresolved with explicit findings. A base reviewer cannot declare RUBRIC_AMBIGUITY to dodge a decision; only the tie-break reviewer may.
independence: Two or three isolated reviewer calls from the same model family are NOT a statistically independent human population. WELP may describe them only as independently isolated blinded adjudications. The protocol must not claim independent human review, an independent evaluator population, or statistically independent annotators. Recorded provenance per reviewer: evaluator id and kind (agent reviewers are never labeled human), independence and blinding declarations, previous-review visibility for tie-breaks, the frozen rubric hash, the reviewed-bytes hash, the prompt-bytes hash where required, and the retained rationale and quotes. Provenance proves binding, not truth.
missing_review: Fewer than two bound independent reviews leave the target unresolved load-bearing review; no model verdict is derived from unadjudicated subjective evidence.
compatibility: Prospective for campaigns under snapshots from welp-next-snapshot-2026-09-24-review-and-setup-hardening onward. Retained campaign evidence under older frozen snapshots stays immutable; re-adjudication of retained raw review evidence under this rule is permitted only when the raw reviewed bytes, prompt bytes and frozen rubric hash are unchanged and every retained review re-binds under this contract, recorded in a new linked event. Historical disagreement outcomes are never relabeled.
mechanical_limit: This contract validates adjudication records and their provenance; it does not make any reviewer correct. Blinding and binding are enforced mechanically; the substance of a judgment is not verifiable by hash.
